title: UPI Turns 10: India's Digital Payment System Logs 12,000-Fold Growth in a Decade
excerpt: From 2 crore transactions in its first year to over 24,000 crore in FY 2025-26, UPI now accounts for 49% of global real-time payments.
body:
• UPI transaction volume surged from 2 crore in FY 2016-17 to over 24,162 crore in FY 2025-26 — a nearly 12,000-fold increase.
  • India now accounts for 49% of all global real-time digital payments, with over 700 banks on the platform.
  • UPI operates in eight countries including the UAE, Singapore, and France, enabling cross-border remittances for the Indian diaspora.

India's Unified Payments Interface completed a decade on August 25, marking ten years since the National Payments Corporation of India launched the system that would fundamentally rewire how the country pays. The numbers tell the story: annual transaction volume jumped from 2 crore in FY 2016-17 to over 24,162 crore in FY 2025-26, while transaction value rose from ₹0.07 lakh crore to approximately ₹314 lakh crore over the same period.

From Pilot to Global Benchmark

When UPI launched on August 25, 2016, 21 banks participated and monthly transactions barely crossed 1 lakh. By July 2026, the platform recorded 2,366 crore transactions in a single month — the highest in its history — with 703 banks live on the network.

The International Monetary Fund has recognized UPI as the world's largest real-time payment system by transaction volume. India now accounts for 49% of all global real-time digital payments, according to the Finance Ministry.

“A domestic worker can send money across states in seconds using a basic smartphone. In this system, the divide between urban and rural, formal and informal, steadily disappears.”

— Government of India, Finance Ministry Statement

The Growth Trajectory

UPI's adoption curve followed a pattern familiar to network effects. Early growth was modest: 91.5 crore transactions in FY 2017-18, rising to 539 crore in FY 2018-19. The pandemic proved to be an inflection point. Contactless payment preferences pushed volumes to 2,233 crore in FY 2020-21, and the momentum never reversed. Volumes more than doubled to 8,375 crore in FY 2022-23, then climbed to 13,013 crore in FY 2023-24.

Monthly transaction value now exceeds ₹28 lakh crore — roughly 70% of India's total currency in circulation, underscoring the scale of digital displacement of cash transactions.

The platform serves approximately 400 million active users, with about 250 million transacting daily, according to industry estimates. Merchant acceptance has expanded in lockstep: UPI QR codes grew 15% year-on-year to 731 million in 2025, while point-of-sale terminals increased to 11.48 million.

Beyond Payments

UPI has evolved beyond simple peer-to-peer transfers. Autopay mandates — recurring payments for subscriptions, EMIs, and utilities — have crossed 100 million setups, with approximately 500 million monthly autopay debits. The platform now underpins credit disbursement, insurance premium collection, and investment flows.

“UPI has successfully decoupled digital payments from high-end hardware and high-income brackets to driving genuine financial inclusion across the country.”

— Rahul Chari, Co-founder and CTO, PhonePe

Going Global

UPI's international footprint has expanded to eight countries: the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius, and Qatar. These integrations facilitate cross-border transactions and remittances — a feature of direct relevance to the millions of Indians working abroad.

The next target is ambitious. Industry executives project UPI will reach one billion users within the coming decade, driven by expansion into rural areas, credit-on-UPI products, and deeper international linkages. While percentage growth rates may moderate as the base expands, absolute volume additions remain substantial: the platform added over 5,000 crore transactions between FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26 alone.

The government's anniversary statement framed UPI's significance in broader terms: “A homegrown system, built in under a decade, now leads the world. What began as an effort to include the unbanked has become the global gold standard for real-time payments.”
